title: Arnold Metoyer, the great trumpeter who was drinking
summary: Metoyer, who played with Ringling Brothers, had astonishing tone and control but was going downhill, so management put Hightower in his chair.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: He looks a little bit like, his pictures look like Peter Boccage almost.
Some pictures I've seen of him, he looks a little bit like Peter Boccage.

Yeah, well, you wouldn't know whether he was a white or what he was, see. But, at those, just around that time he was turning, he was turning to that wine, that drinking, see. One of the greatest trumpet players that ever was. He played with number one Ringling Brothers band, the white band. He sat in the band. And when Zoo carried me there, he always says, a trumpet player? So and so was the case, and he passed me on the show, he said, come on, sit down, here's my horn. That just gave him a chance to go walk around and get his bucket together, see. All musicians that didn't hold up had a bucket, you know. And they drank a claret wine, take a dime. Well, that's where Alno was going down at, just during that time, see. But at the same time, he was one of the greatest I've ever seen, because he could take his horn and hang it up by the vowels. And hang that horn straight, test it for time after time. And he could put his lips up to that horn and let you take a piece of thread and pass through that horn and you'd never hear the blemish of that tone. So I played down there one night in his place practically all night. So after then, it looked like it got set on me. Mr. Groschel told Pierones that it would be better to put me in the band because half the time they couldn't ever see Alno, they didn't know where he was at, see. And he had a wife and I think four children, four of them. So dear
